Subject: Security form initiation and evidence mapping — follow-up

Hi Marta / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — appreciate the level-setting and the specific compliance asks. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the procurement path: 

Call recap (high level)
- You’re starting vendor security intake for WellSpring’s new patient-engagement feature; primary concerns are SOC 2 status, HIPAA scope for PHI handling, and encryption/data residency.
- You use a standard SIG questionnaire but are open to a prefilled CAIQ or our custom matrix if that speeds review.

Proposed next steps
1) Do you prefer a SIG XLSX for your vendor portal, or would a prefilled CAIQ (JSON) be easier? We can provide both; just need to know which to upload.
2) I’ve attached a draft prefill (redwood_sig_prefill.xlsx) and a short SOC 2 progress summary (soc2-progress-summary.pdf). If you want, we can pre-populate your SIG and mark items that will require evidence.
3) A couple of clarifying questions from our side to ensure accurate prefill (answers will determine evidence mapping):
   - Will you be processing PHI as defined by HIPAA (e.g., patient identifiers plus clinical data) or only PII?
   - Do you have a minimum acceptable data residency requirement (US-only, EU acceptable, other)?
   - What is your expected evidence turnaround for artifacts (7 business days, 15, 30)?

Technical notes (short)
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently in-scope for SOC 2 Type II; control testing started 2026-08-01 with final report expected Q1 2027. The attached PDF has more detail.
- HIPAA: We support BAA relationships; we can scope specific product endpoints that will handle PHI and provide technical and administrative controls summary.

If you can confirm SIG vs CAIQ preference and the three clarifying items above, we’ll prefill and route any outstanding evidence requests to your procurement portal. Suggested timeline: get your preference + clarifications by EOD Oct 2, we prefill by Oct 7, and provide evidence packet (~7–10 business days after prefill acceptance).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if that helps triage.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced: redwood_sig_prefill.xlsx (draft), soc2-progress-summary.pdf (summary), dataflow-diagram.png (illustrative)

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications so we can route appropriately on our side: 

1) PHI: yes — the feature will process PHI (patient identifiers + clinical notes). We will need a BAA and specific HIPAA scoping.
2) Data residency: US-only for PHI; non-PHI analytics data can be EU/US.
3) Evidence turnaround: procurement expects artifacts within 10 business days after we receive the prefilled SIG. Is that feasible?

Also: we prefer SIG in XLSX format for our vendor portal. If you can prefill that, great — call out any items that require SOC 2 artifacts or third-party attestations.

Two more technical asks from our security team: encryption-at-rest specifics (algorithm, KMS provider), and confirmation on whether Redwood uses subcontractors for logging/monitoring that might see PHI.

If you can send a consolidated prefill + answers to encryption/KMS/subprocessor questions, we’ll initiate our internal review.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager | WellSpring Health

Hi Marta — appreciate the quick turnaround. Below is a consolidated response and attached prefill bundle. I’ve included Soojin (security) and Ben (technical owner) on this thread for any follow-up.

Answers to your technical questions (summary):
- PHI / BAA: Yes — we can enter into a BAA. We will scope the BAA to the product endpoints that will process PHI and include appropriate administrative and technical controls.
- Data residency: We will restrict PHI to US-only. Non-PHI analytics can be stored in US/EU (configurable).
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 encryption for data at rest. Keys are managed via AWS KMS (customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private deployments). We can attach KMS configuration screenshots and the key rotation policy excerpt.
- Subprocessors: We use a small set of subprocessors for observability and logging (e.g., LogStream Systems) — they operate under contract and with limited access controls; we will include the subprocessor list and their SOC 2/state of compliance in the evidence packet. We do not share PHI with downstream subprocessors except where explicitly provisioned in a BAA and with technical controls.
- Evidence turnaround: We can routinely assemble the prefill and SOC 2 artifact packet for review within 7–10 business days after you accept the prefilled SIG. If specific items require legal review, it may extend to ~15 business days.

Attached: redwood_sig_prefill.xlsx (prefilled answers, flagged items), soc2-progress-summary.pdf (timeline and what controls are covered), dataflow-diagram.png (high level).

Next steps
1) Please confirm you received the prefill and whether procurement wants us to upload directly to your portal.
2) If you want a short 20–30 minute session to walk the security team through the packet, we’re happy to set that up — propose Oct 6 or Oct 7 morning PT.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for confirmation and to move the prefill into your portal.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
